prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down indoor view where a crouching child's head and hair bun are the nearest surfaces at roughly 0.4–0.6 metres below and in front of the camera wearer, while the child's shoulders, limbs, and the open red-and-white book on the rug sit slightly farther at about 0.7–1.0 metres, all within arm's reach of both the child and the camera wearer. Behind and above the child in the image plane, storage bins and a dark shelving unit against the wall lie about 1.2–2.0 metres away, with the child's head partially occluding her lower body and the floor directly beneath her. Across the five frames, the bright blob of the child's head rises and shifts slightly from bottom-left toward the upper-left/centre as she lifts her torso and turns her head rightward toward the open book, always facing down and away from the camera wearer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground child and raised open book page from the busy patterned rug and dark shelving cubbies, though it is unreliable along wispy hair edges and inside the dark shelf recesses where depth values blur and drop out.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the crouching child in the lower-left foreground (about 0.4–0.9 metres away) and the rectangular storage bin of books just behind her to the right (about 1.2–1.5 metres away), while omitting the open book on the floor, the rug, and the shelving unit. In frame 1, the child's patterned shirt is mislabelled as a 'backpack' while she is bent low and partly cut off by the bottom frame edge; in frame 2, she is missed entirely, and only in frames 3–5 is she segmented as 'person' as she rises slightly and turns her head rightward toward the floor book without looking at the camera wearer. Across frames 1 to 5, stacked books on the upper shelf (1.5 metres away) and books inside the floor bins (within the child's reach at ~0.5–0.8 metres from her) are intermittently segmented as 'book'. While the masks help delineate the contours of the book bin and the child's upper profile against the dark background in later frames, the map is highly unreliable: it misses the child in frames 1–2, splits her body into two 'person' instances and a false 'tie' mask on her leg in frame 4, and labels the entire storage bin as a single 'book'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons for either the camera wearer or the child crouching roughly 0.4–0.9 metres below and in front of the camera. In the RGB strip, the child is seen from a steep top-down angle with her head and hair bun occluding much of her torso, her face turned downward and then slightly right toward an open book within her arm's reach on the rug (about 0.3 metres to her right), and her lower legs partly cut off at the bottom-left frame edge. Over the five frames, she lifts her head and upper body slightly while her hands and feet remain near the floor and the open book. Because the steep overhead viewpoint and self-occlusion by the child's head and hair cause total pose estimation failure, this map provides no spatial information beyond what is visible in RGB and is completely unreliable here.
